You're vastly over-estimating the quality of the internet in most of the world. Streaming video can get away with hiding the problems because it can buffer parts of the video to make up for network problems. Streaming a game means every button press you make has to go to the server over the internet, the server processes what your button press did, and then it sends it back to you, where your device renders it.

Even if you are lucky enough to have a 40ms ping to one of these streaming servers, you end up with an additional 80ms of delay just to get your key press back to your screen. And any lag or network problems, your key and button presses get delayed.

Streaming games is a pipe dream for publishers, because it completely centralizes everything and gives them absolute power over everything. Specially in situations where older games are hurting new game sales, like new sports game, annual releases, etc. It will end used game sales, and when you are a company like Ubisoft who loves to shit out the same game with a few minor tweaks every year, killing the used game market is a big deal for you.
